fact_check_log.claim: Cutlery is laid in the order it will be used, working from the outside in.
Forks to the left, knives and spoons to the right (body and takeaway 2).
Oyster fork is the one exception, set to the right if used.
Each knife set with its blade facing inward toward the plate.
Only set the cutlery your guests will use (body and takeaway 1).
Dessert cutlery arrives with dessert or sits above the plate, fork handle left, spoon above with handle right (body and FAQ).
Most traditional setting: dessert spoon above the dessert fork.
Setting dessert cutlery from the start saves a cutlery run at dessert (insider detail).
Water glass above the knife or slightly to its right (body and takeaway 2 'glasses above the knives').
Wine glasses, one or perhaps two at a less formal dinner, to the right of the water glass; formal cascade to the right (body and FAQ).
Butter knife rests across the bread plate, blade facing inward toward the diner, handle pointing right (body and FAQ).
Bread plate sits upper left, above the forks: written as living practice, no origin, per source pack must_include note.
Charger plate may be used or left out (body and FAQ).
Charger stays through early courses and first-course plate is cleared with each course.
Napkin to the left of the forks or centred on the charger; fork on napkin is a matter of style (body and FAQ).
Clearing for dessert: unused cutlery, bread plate and butter knife removed, dessert cutlery stays if set.
Finger bowls come out after a messy course rather than sitting at the place all meal.
Name card at the top of the setting, above the plate or on the napkin; menu on the charger or beside the name card: styling advice, no origin, per source pack.
Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit (brand-facts claims list).
One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact (brand-facts claims list).
